# @lidtop/opencode-cost

See where your usage and time go: recorded costs and tokens across projects and models, with daily activity over time, plus how long agents worked, how long they waited on you, and how much ran in parallel. Costs come from OpenCode's provider-reported records, not a separate pricing table.

[![Watch the Cost demo: a month of cost, tokens, and agent time by model, project, day, and longest turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZackarySantana/opcode/main/docs/images/cost-demo.jpg)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5bb36ebf-b44d-41e9-8d1c-3b442618cb3b)

*The 36-second demo uses a sample month of usage.*

![Cost dashboard with usage totals, model and project breakdowns, and daily activity ordered newest first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZackarySantana/opcode/main/docs/images/cost-dashboard.png)

## Install

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0 or newer in the 2.x line**.

```sh
opencode plugin add @lidtop/opencode-cost
```

Or add it to `plugins` in your global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (or `opencode.json`), keeping your existing entries:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@lidtop/opencode-cost"]
}
```

**Where it runs.** Install it globally so the server collector is available across projects. The server records usage and owns the database; the terminal and desktop dashboards query it over plugin RPC (every part uses the ID `opcode-cost`). A client-only install in `cli.json` cannot supply that RPC service, so the dashboard needs the server plugin enabled at the connected location. OpenCode Desktop reads plugins only from `opencode.json(c)`.

## Use

Run `/cost` or select **Cost** in the command palette. It opens a dialog with five tabs:

- **Overview:** the totals. **Recorded messages**, input, output, reasoning, cache-read, and cache-write tokens, and USD cost when there is any; then **agent time** and turn count, **waiting on you**, and **parallel** time with its peak.
- **Models**, **Projects**, and **Daily:** one row per provider/model and variant, project, or date. Each row shows its usage, with a bar, and its time: agent time, turns, and waiting. Models and projects rank by cost, then tokens, followed by any with time but no usage, by agent time; dates are newest first.
- **Turns:** the eight longest turns, with title, project, model, start, and duration.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `tab` / `shift+tab` | Switch tabs (or click a tab) |
| `↑` / `↓`, `j` / `k` | Select a row; the list scrolls to keep it in view. On the Overview, scroll |
| `enter` | Turns tab: close the dialog and open the selected turn's session (or click it) |
| `d` | Date range: today, last 7 days, last 30 days, or all time |
| `/` | Search the current tab's rows |
| `r` | Refresh and reconcile the current project's complete history; retry failed imports |
| `esc` | Leave the search box, clear the search, close the date picker, then close the dialog |

Totals are never narrowed: the search narrows only the rows shown. The date range applies to every tab and is shown before the search box; reopening `/cost` starts again from the last 30 days. The view rereads the server ledger every five seconds while open and shortly after public usage updates. Date ranges use the **server's local calendar**, include today, and attribute usage to message creation time and turns to their start. A project is named after its most recently used directory and includes its recorded worktrees.

**Tokens, and cost when there is any.** Amounts show cost and tokens (`$2.00  15 tok`), and bars follow cost. With no recorded cost in the range, as on a subscription, the cost card is dropped and everything is shown and sized by tokens. The rule covers the whole dialog, never single rows, so a free model beside paid ones reads `$0.00` with an empty bar.

### Desktop

In OpenCode Desktop, a titlebar pill shows **today's spend** on the app's own server (or today's tokens when nothing recorded a cost); click it, select **Cost** in the command palette, or run `/cost` to open the dashboard. It has the same sections as the terminal's tabs (Overview, Models, Projects, Daily, and Turns, as tables with bars) and the same date ranges, starting from the last 30 days. Click a turn's title to open its session. The pill and an open dashboard reread shortly after the server records usage (the server emits a throttled `updated` RPC event) and every minute; **Refresh** rereads at once.

The desktop app does not import history: only the terminal does (see [Collection and history](#collection-and-history)), so usage from before the server plugin was enabled appears once a terminal has opened the project.

## Time

"Where did my time go?" Only **root sessions** are timed; a subagent's work is part of its parent's turn, so it is never counted twice. Sessions an Opcode plugin starts beside yours, such as [Review](../review/README.md)'s questions about a diff, aren't timed either, though their usage and cost count.

- **Turn (agent time):** from the user prompt, or the moment queued input is delivered, until the session goes idle. A prompt steered in while the agent works belongs to the same turn. A turn woken without a prompt, such as by a background subagent finishing, starts at its first recorded step.
- **Waiting on you:** from a turn going idle until the next user prompt in that session, counting at most **30 minutes** per wait so nights away do not count. A turn woken without a prompt leaves no waiting gap. Waits are summed per session, so two sessions waiting at once count twice. A wait belongs to the turn it follows.
- **Parallel:** time with two or more root sessions in a turn at once, and the most at any moment.
- **Model:** each turn is attributed to the provider/model and variant whose steps produced the most output and reasoning tokens. Turns with no recorded step show as "no recorded step", a row with time but no usage.
- **Dates:** a turn belongs to the server's local date on which it started, like usage to message creation.

How times are derived: OpenCode history stores each delivered user prompt as a user message and each finished execution as an idle message, both at the moment of the underlying event. The server records the same moments live from `session.inbox.delivered` (user input only) and `session.execution.succeeded`, `failed`, or `interrupted`, so live collection and import agree without double counting. Import sends just these timestamps, never prompt text. Step times come from the same assistant records as costs.

Limitations:

- Time waiting on a permission or question prompt inside a turn counts as agent time.
- History has no idle marker for a server shutdown mid-turn (live collection records one). Without it, the turn ends at its last recorded step or prompt if the next prompt arrives more than 30 minutes later; otherwise it runs until the next idle. The same rule splits a turn when you steer in a prompt after more than 30 minutes without a step of its own, for example while a long subagent runs.
- A running turn counts up to its latest recorded step or prompt.
- A fork's history before the fork was created is not timed again.

## Collection and history

The server records completed and failed assistant steps, including headless usage, completed compactions with model metadata, and the prompt and idle moments of root sessions. It filters the cross-location event stream against each session's directory, reconnects after the stream ends, and cancels outstanding work on unload.

Historical import runs when the terminal plugin loads or changes location, and on `r`. A server plugin cannot list message history in OpenCode 2.2.0, so the terminal reads all assistant, compaction, user, and idle pages for **every session in the current project, including other worktrees**, extracts usage metadata and turn timestamps, and sends validated batches of at most 100 items to the server. The server derives project, session, title, and location identity from its own session lookup. Prompts and summaries are never sent.

- **Safe to repeat:** imports are cancellable and idempotent, and each batch is atomic. Changing location cancels the previous import; a failure is shown only while its location is current. Retries scan again without double-counting, and old completion markers never permanently skip reconciliation. Projects never opened in a terminal are not imported until opened.
- **Live wins:** history never overwrites a message collected live. For legacy or historical records, only a later completion timestamp replaces existing values, and incomplete snapshots cannot erase completed usage. Duplicate live updates replace existing values; older live events are ignored. A failed step that reports no usage keeps any usage already recorded for its message.
- **Moves and forks:** message identity stays stable when OpenCode moves a session between projects, and reconciliation updates its attribution without touching protected costs. Forks can inherit their parent's message IDs; each ID is billed once, stays attributed to the first recorded session, and later duplicates are skipped without blocking the rest of the batch.

## Accounting

- Costs come directly from OpenCode records; there is no provider pricing table or price recalculation.
- A recorded message is an assistant step or an eligible completed compaction, not a user turn and not necessarily one provider request. Incomplete or failed steps can be recorded with zero usage. Title and transient generation are not collected separately, so this is not an exhaustive invoice.
- Missing, non-finite, or negative usage values count as zero.
- Public events have no replay: reconnecting alone cannot recover missed usage, so use `r` to reconcile. Records deleted from OpenCode before collection or import cannot be recovered.
- Recorded usage remains after its session is deleted. There is no pruning, budget alerts, export, or billing integration.

## Options

Set a custom database path on the **server**:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "@lidtop/opencode-cost", "options": { "database": "/absolute/path/cost.sqlite" } }
  ]
}
```

- `database`: where the ledger is stored. Relative paths resolve from the server's OpenCode state directory. `:memory:` works but is not durable. With a remote server, paths and environment variables belong to that machine. The default is `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/opencode-cost/cost.sqlite` (or `~/.local/state/opencode/opencode-cost/cost.sqlite`).

## Data and privacy

**Only the server opens SQLite.** The terminal never reads or writes a local cost database, so a remote dashboard shows the **connected server's ledger**, and imported remote history stays on that server. Local and remote histories are never mixed.

The database stores IDs, directories, root-session titles, model, variant, and provider IDs, timestamps, costs, and token counts only: no prompts, responses, tool arguments, file contents, or credentials. Full history is fetched transiently for metadata extraction. To clear history, stop OpenCode and remove the database and its SQLite sidecars; there is no delete action in the dashboard.

## Replacing opencode-cost

The default database path is the same as `opencode-cost`'s, but the schema is not compatible: stop OpenCode and remove an existing database and its SQLite sidecars before enabling this plugin, then let the import rebuild history. Remove the old plugin too, to avoid competing collectors and `/cost` commands.

## Development

From the repository root:

```sh
mise exec -- bun test plugins/cost/test
mise exec -- bun run typecheck
mise run dev cost
```

The build bundles the private `@opcode/core`, `@opcode/tabs`, and `@opcode/ui` workspaces into the package; OpenCode, OpenTUI, and Solid stay external.

# @lidtop/opencode-cost

## 0.5.0

### Minor Changes

- b4b8592: Sessions an Opcode plugin starts beside yours, such as Review's questions about a diff, count toward usage and cost but not toward agent time, turns, or parallel time.

### Patch Changes

- 9c2b277: The shared card list every plugin bundles can show a pane beside the list, which Snippets uses for its preview. Nothing changes for this plugin.
- 2540a17: Rebuilt with the shared dialog components, whose Settings tab now draws its choices with a component GH PR Status also uses. Nothing visible changes.

## 0.4.0

### Minor Changes

- 57063c7: Add an OpenCode Desktop part: a titlebar pill with today's spend, and a Cost dashboard (command palette and `/cost`) with the terminal's totals, models, projects, days, and longest turns. The server emits a throttled `updated` RPC event when it records usage.
- 62c9603: Require OpenCode 2.2.0 and OpenTUI 0.7.

## 0.3.3

### Patch Changes

- 5ccffe8: Shared code moved into helpers every plugin bundles: the refresh schedule now also works outside the terminal, and there are new helpers for state shared by a server's projects, RPC contracts and handlers, and following a server's state. For Context, Feed, Later, and Media nothing changes. In Cost, Review, Snippets, and Sessions, a call the terminal aborted is no longer reported as a failure. In Sessions, every project open on a server now shares one search index connection and one writer per database file, rather than possibly one per project.
- e91635a: Shared code that Feed and GH PR Status use moved into helpers every plugin bundles: the minute clock that ages views, and sending changes to the server in order while showing them at once. Nothing changes for any plugin.

## 0.3.2

### Patch Changes

- abc551c: The shared live-event helper can now resubscribe to an event stream that stops delivering, for the Sessions sidebar. No behavior changes.

## 0.3.1

### Patch Changes

- e5df44d: The README opens with a short demo video.

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- 2b142b5: `/cost` is now a dialog, like `/feed` and `/ghpr`, with one search box and an in-dialog date range picker (`d`). Opening a longest turn closes the dialog and opens its session. Amounts show tokens beside cost; a view with no recorded cost, as on a subscription, hides cost and shows only tokens, and breakdowns rank cost ties by tokens.
- 3f3b12d: `/cost` has Overview, Models, Projects, Daily, and Turns tabs instead of panels stacked in one view. The Overview holds every total; each breakdown row shows its usage and its time together, and lists every model (now split by variant, as on the time side), project, and date in the range rather than the top eight or newest 14. ↑/↓ select rows one at a time and scroll to keep the selection in view; enter on a turn still opens its session. The date range (`d`) is the only filter: the project and model pickers and `x` reset are gone, along with the server's project/model filter parameters and picker options.
- 47f719c: Add time to `/cost`: agent working time per turn, time waiting on you (at most 30 minutes per wait), parallel time across root sessions with its peak, breakdowns by model/variant, project, and day, and the longest turns, which open their session. Delete the existing Cost database and its SQLite sidecars before upgrading; the history import rebuilds usage and backfills turn timing.

### Patch Changes

- 0c50ac8: Keep the Overview cards inside the `/cost` dialog, and leave a blank line between rows in the list tabs.
- bb097fd: Require OpenCode 2.1.3 or newer.
- 1708674: Move Later's prompt paste helper into the shared UI package so Snippets can reuse it. No behavior changes.
- 44bad65: The Pull requests and Feeds sidebar sections show their refresh countdown beside the title instead of on a line of their own. Those sections and Agents no longer add a line saying there's nothing to show; they show just the title.
- f27f920: The shared item card can lead with its title when an item has no head, for Later. No behavior changes.

## 0.2.4

### Patch Changes

- 439c23e: Tag the package with the `opencode` and `opencode-plugin` npm keywords so plugin directories such as OpenDock can list it.

## 0.2.3

### Patch Changes

- a8e520d: Standardize the package READMEs: install with `opencode plugin add` first, show screenshots, and use the same sections and wording across every plugin.

## 0.2.2

### Patch Changes

- e6b5093: Context no longer lets missing, negative, or non-finite provider usage values corrupt its token totals. History pagination, live-event reconnection, and usage normalization now behave consistently across plugins, and Cost always closes its ledger on unload. Errors with an empty message now show a readable fallback instead of a blank notification.
- 6eaeb52: Context and Cost now share one coalesced refresh from the bundled core utilities. Cost dashboard reads time out after 30 seconds instead of blocking later refreshes, and refresh-failure warnings in both stay visible until a retry succeeds. Later and Sessions only rebuild against the updated shared core.
- ea7786e: Send the history message-type filter only on the first page, so sessions with many assistant messages import without the cursor being rejected.
- 2c29af6: History import now asks the server only for assistant and compaction messages, and briefly reuses the last session authorization instead of re-checking it for every batch.
- 0eb7423: Switching location now cancels the previous location's history import, and an import failure is shown only for the location it happened in; `r` retries the current location.
- 937ef26: Keep recorded cost when a retried step later fails without reporting usage, instead of overwriting it with zero.
- b7779fb: Show the actual reason when a server-side cost request fails, and stop slow session lookups from delaying dashboard reads and live collection.
- 2ae4cb3: Aggregate the dashboard in SQLite rather than scanning every recorded message, and label each project by its most recently used directory.
- 1ae9d93: Create new Cost and Later databases owner-only (0600 files in a 0700 directory) before SQLite writes to them, as Sessions already did; existing database permissions are left unchanged. All plugins now share one XDG state-path resolver.
- e70e939: Measure and truncate labels with the host renderer's width method in every plugin, so Cost project, model, and warning labels no longer overflow with wide characters such as CJK or emoji. Cost, Later, and Sessions keyboard hints with a matching command are now clickable, and all views take their colors from the shared theme palette.

## 0.2.1

### Patch Changes

- da30824: Show the cost dashboard's daily activity newest date first while retaining the latest 14 dates and complete usage totals.

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 805bb55: Publish independently versioned OpenCode V2 plugins with bundled private helpers and terminal extensions.

### Patch Changes

- 8f1a01b: Balance theme colors: use normal foreground for page/dialog titles and shortcut keys, muted labels and neutral borders, accent hues for sections/charts, and interactive hues for values. Preserve the theme's contrasting selection foreground/background pair.
- 4b98516: Show project paths instead of opaque project IDs beside names in the cost dashboard's project picker, matching the Sessions browser. Keep filtering by stable project ID across worktrees.
- 572b6e9: Restore consistent theme-aware colors for headings, borders, metrics, keyboard hints, charts, and statuses. Follow live light/dark theme changes and preserve dialog and selection colors.
